grade.first_issue: No decisive defect; no grading rule imposes a cap.
grade.summary: The proof is complete and correct. The lexicographically decreasing pair (S,C) establishes finite termination, including the case gcd(m,n)=1. Primewise, the gcd of all valuation coordinates is invariant because the selected pair (x,y) becomes (min(x,y),|x-y|), which has the same gcd. At termination, the invariant rules out all entries being 1, so exactly one entry M exceeds 1, and its prime exponents are uniquely determined by the initial board.
strengths: Correctly computes the change in the total number of prime factors counted with multiplicity.
Uses a valid well-founded lexicographic descent to prove termination.
Correctly identifies and proves the primewise valuation-gcd invariant.
Correctly reconstructs the unique terminal value M from its prime exponents.
